prerequisites: The student must have successfully completed module examinations amounting to 120 ECTS credits. Exceptions are decided by the examination board upon student's request (cf. §14 (1) of the SPO).

learning_outcomes.text: The student can independently work on a delimited, subject-relevant topic within a given timeframe according to scientific criteria.
He/she is able to research, analyze information, abstract it, and compile and recognize fundamental principles and laws from less structured information.
He/she can survey a problem, select scientific methods and procedures, and use them to solve it or identify further potential. This generally also considers social and/or ethical aspects.
He/she can interpret, evaluate, and, if necessary, graphically represent the results obtained.
He/she is able to clearly structure a scientific work and (a) communicate it in written form using technical terminology, and (b) present it orally and discuss it with experts.

assessment_rules: The Bachelor's thesis (12 ECTS) and an oral presentation (3 ECTS) are assessed. The maximum processing time for the thesis is three months. The topic can only be returned once within the first month. An extension of up to one month may be granted by the examination board upon justified request. If the thesis is not submitted on time, it is graded 'not sufficient' (5.0), unless the student is not responsible for the delay. The thesis is evaluated by at least two examiners. In case of differing evaluations, the examination board sets the grade or may appoint another expert. The evaluation must be completed within six weeks after submission. The presentation, lasting about 20 minutes, should take place no later than six weeks after the thesis submission and is followed by a discussion with the audience.
